publicationPolicy: Precise, bounded verification only. Original files were visually reviewed via the official public source; no raw file checksum was captured. These cases NEVER by themselves close the 55 local gaps or nine national blockers.

cases.method: Manually inspected official county PDF page 2 and statewide official-list PDF pages 1–2, matching candidate, office, election year, county and vote totals between two independently formatted reports of the same issuing authority.
cases.boundedConclusion: For these two candidate/county totals, the two New Jersey Division of Elections reports agree. This is a cross-report numerical reconciliation, not an independently certified nationwide dataset.
limits: Two publications of the same issuing authority are not independent organizations.
Full all-candidate and 21-county summation, signed canvass/certification status, later corrections, original-file hashes and other contests have not been independently checked.
No electoral inference, candidate ranking or causal political-finance connection is established.

cases.method: Read operator's dated fare-index page and linked official Northern Interstate tariff PDF, then cross-reference two-zone row and adult one-way column.
cases.boundedConclusion: NJ TRANSIT's 2026 adjusted fare materials identify $4.20 for adult one-way travel in the two-zone Northern Interstate fare category.
limits: Without official origin-to-destination zone mapping, a published fare category does not establish the price of any particular journey.
No historical price-change calculation, toll comparison, service frequency or household cost attribution established.
Original PDF SHA256 and any superseding tariff revision were not recorded.

cases.method: Read latest repository sitewide audit report; only the referenced 46 HTML files and 333 JSON files were in the audited snapshot.
cases.boundedConclusion: The reported sitewide static scan found zero unresolved static references in the inspected repository snapshot.
limits: A static scan does not prove that third-party websites, live API requests, dynamic browser interactions or public Vercel routes always work.
Audit results come from project CI, not a second independent internet/browser test.
The full frontend reliability gap remains open.
